canonical_definition: Code Generation is the ability to synthesize correct, executable code or programs from natural language prompts, task descriptions, or partial specifications, often operationalized through correctness criteria such as passing predefined tests (e.g., HumanEval, MBPP) or producing functionally valid implementations. While most definitions emphasize program synthesis for general programming tasks, some extend to code completion, patch generation, or domain-specific applications (e.g., SQL, PyTorch models), with varying focus on single-turn generation versus iterative refinement with feedback. Disagreements arise in scope, ranging from narrow benchmarks to broader practical coding proficiency.
